# A. LENTIC SPECIES

```{r}
MJaccard_Lentic <- read.csv("01_DATA/04_Data_Analysis/01_Lentic/MJacc_lentic.csv", row.names = 1)
head(MJaccard_Lentic)
```

```{r}
class(MJaccard_Lentic)
```

```{r}
jaccard_matrix <- as.matrix(MJaccard_Lentic)
class(jaccard_matrix)
```

```{r}
all(rownames(jaccard_matrix) == colnames(jaccard_matrix))  # debe ser TRUE
```


```{r}
setdiff(rownames(jaccard_matrix), colnames(jaccard_matrix))
setdiff(colnames(jaccard_matrix), rownames(jaccard_matrix))

```

```{r}
# Obtain the species that are in both rows and columns
species_common <- intersect(rownames(jaccard_matrix), colnames(jaccard_matrix))

# Subset and reorder
jaccard_matrix <- jaccard_matrix[species_common, species_common]

```

```{r}
all(rownames(jaccard_matrix) == colnames(jaccard_matrix))  # now it should be TRUE
```

## Co-occurrence

```{r}
# Read co-occurrence data
cooc_df <- read.csv("01_Data/04_Data_Analysis/01_Lentic/lentic_lentic_cooccurrence.csv")
head(cooc_df)
```

```{r}
cooc_df <- cooc_df[complete.cases(cooc_df), ]

# Ensure that species names are listed as factors or characters.
cooc_df$sp1 <- as.character(cooc_df$sp1)
cooc_df$sp2 <- as.character(cooc_df$sp2)

```


```{r}
# Extract all unique species (from both columns)
all_species <- sort(unique(c(cooc_df$sp1, cooc_df$sp2)))

# Create empty array initialised to 0
cooc_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(all_species), ncol = length(all_species),
                      dimnames = list(all_species, all_species))

# Fill the matrix with the values of the number of shared grids
for (i in 1:nrow(cooc_df)) {
  sp1 <- cooc_df$sp1[i]
  sp2 <- cooc_df$sp2[i]
  val <- cooc_df$cooccurrence_cells[i]
  
  if (sp1 %in% all_species && sp2 %in% all_species) {
    cooc_matrix[sp1, sp2] <- val
    cooc_matrix[sp2, sp1] <- val
  } else {
    warning(paste("Species not found:", sp1, sp2))
  }
}
```

```{r}
all_species
```


```{r}
setdiff(unique(c(cooc_df$sp1, cooc_df$sp2)), all_species)
```

## Do both matrices have the same species?

```{r}
common_species <- intersect(rownames(jaccard_matrix), rownames(cooc_matrix))
length(common_species)  # must be > 2 for the test to work

# Subset both matrices with the same order
jaccard_sub <- jaccard_matrix[common_species, common_species]
cooc_sub <- cooc_matrix[common_species, common_species]

```

## MENTEL TEST

```{r}
# We convert to ‘dist’ objects
jaccard_dist <- as.dist(1 - jaccard_sub)  # converts similarity to distance
cooc_dist <- as.dist(cooc_sub)            # is now a valid measure (number of shared cells)

# Mantel test
mantel_result <- mantel(cooc_dist, jaccard_dist, method = "pearson", permutations = 999)

# Result
print(mantel_result)
```

r = -0.83 indicates a very strong negative correlation between the two matrices.

The matrices are:

- cooc_matrix: number of cells shared between pairs of species.

- jaccard_sub: niche similarity, converted to distance (1 - Jaccard).

Therefore:

- The greater the niche distance (the less similar the niches are), the greater the co-occurrence.

- This contradicts the typical ecological expectation (that species with more similar niches co-occur more).


```{r}
cooc_vec <- as.vector(cooc_dist)
jaccard_vec <- as.vector(jaccard_dist)

# Create dataframe
df_plot <- data.frame(
  jaccard = jaccard_vec,
  cooccurrence = cooc_vec
)

# plot
plot1 <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = jaccard, y = cooccurrence)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 4, size = 1.2, shape = 16, color = "#a6cee3") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#1f78b4", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Intra-lentic: Niche vs Co-occurrence",
    x = "Niche distance (1 - Jaccard)",
    y = "Spatial co-occurrence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
plot1
```

```{r}
#ggsave("04_Figures/plot1_Intra_Lentic_mentel.png", plot = plot1, width = 10, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 600)
```

# C. ANALYSIS BETWEEN GROUPS (lentic vs. lotic)

```{r}
MJaccard_all <- read.csv("01_DATA/04_Data_Analysis/03_LenticVSLotic/MJacc_LenticVSLotic.csv", row.names = 1)
```

```{r}
mat_to_long <- function(mat, name) {
  as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(mat))) %>%
    rename(Species1 = Var1, Species2 = Var2, !!name := Freq)
}

df_Jaccard <- mat_to_long(MJaccard_all, "Jaccard")
```

```{r}
species_group <- read_excel("01_Data/03_Data_species/List_of_species.xlsx", sheet = "species_group")
```


```{r}
df_Jaccard <- df_Jaccard %>%
  left_join(species_group %>% rename(Species1 = species, Group1 = group), by = "Species1") %>%
  left_join(species_group %>% rename(Species2 = species, Group2 = group), by = "Species2")

df_Jaccard <- df_Jaccard %>%
  mutate(PairID = paste(Species1, Species2, sep = "_"))

all_pairs <- df_Jaccard$PairID

# Keep only different lentil pairs
df_inter  <- df_Jaccard %>%
  filter(((Group1 == "Lentic" & Group2 == "Lotic") | (Group1 == "Lotic" & Group2 == "Lentic")) & Species1 != Species2)
```

```{r}
colnames(df_inter)
```

```{r}
# Ensure that species names are listed as factors or characters.
df_inter$sp1 <- as.character(df_inter$Species1)
df_inter$sp2 <- as.character(df_inter$Species2)
```


```{r}
# Extract all unique species (from both columns)
all_species <- sort(unique(c(df_inter$sp1, df_inter$sp2)))

# Create empty array initialised to 0
jaccard_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(all_species), ncol = length(all_species),
                      dimnames = list(all_species, all_species))

# Fill the matrix with the values of the number of shared grids
for (i in 1:nrow(df_inter)) {
  sp1 <- df_inter$sp1[i]
  sp2 <- df_inter$sp2[i]
  val <- df_inter$Jaccard[i]
  
  if (sp1 %in% all_species && sp2 %in% all_species) {
    jaccard_matrix[sp1, sp2] <- val
    jaccard_matrix[sp2, sp1] <- val
  } else {
    warning(paste("Species not found:", sp1, sp2))
  }
}
```

```{r}
cooc_df <- read_excel("01_Data/04_Data_Analysis/03_LenticVSLotic/intergroup_cooccurrence.xlsx")
```
